TestPaxosBug::test_synced_most_recent_co.description: Regression for CASSANDRA-12043 (expired most-recent-commit causing endless paxos repair / CAS timeouts). 3 nodes in 3 racks, RF=3, table with paxos_grace_seconds=120. Node C stopped, LWT INSERT IF NOT EXISTS at QUORUM on A+B; after 60s B stopped, C started and a SERIAL read via A (A+C quorum, C missing MRC -> paxos repair); after another 60s (MRC now older than the 120s TTL on A) a second SERIAL read must not time out. Only asserts no exception; returned row not checked.

origin.summary: Lukasz Sojka: cover case from CASSANDRA-12043 (merged as part of PR #2323 'Convert to Pytest').

Paxos state TTL = paxos_grace_seconds (paxos_state.cc:321). Applies to both vnodes (system.paxos) and tablets (<table>$paxos); runs in next-dtest-tablets and next-dtest-consistent-topology, 32/32 passed.

TestPaxosBug::test_synced_most_recent_co.reason: Unique coverage of the expired-MRC paxos repair path (no scylla test exercises replicas_missing_most_recent_commit / paxos_grace_seconds expiry; grep test/cluster, test/boost). Note: only asserts no exception (the CAS-timeout target), never checks the read returns (1,1) (lwt_test.py:800,834). Could be shortened via smaller paxos_grace_seconds.
